prompt: Vertical 9:16 night photograph on 35 mm film, taken from inside a stationary ambulance looking sideways out through its rain-streaked side window at a double-decker bus halted in the next lane, so close that the bus side fills the whole window. The window's dark rubber edge frames the shot on all four sides, a soft blur of the ambulance's interior just visible at the bottom corner. Through the glass, square-on and in sharp focus, is a printed campaign poster stuck to the side of the bus: a smooth, over-retouched portrait of the man from the reference image, his head in the upper half of the poster, phone held to his right ear with his right hand, eyebrows raised, a confident closed-mouth smile, eyes to camera, on a flat pale grey background. Beneath his face, in huge bold white condensed sans-serif capitals on a deep charcoal band across the bottom of the poster, the words "SAVE OUR NHS", no other text, no logo. Light sources: the ambulance's blue emergency lights pulsing across the bus side and turning the raindrops on our window into blue beads, a sodium-orange street lamp overhead washing the top of the poster warm, and the faint cold fluorescent glow of the bus's lower-deck windows above the poster edge. Droplets on the window in the foreground are slightly soft while the poster behind them is crisp; teal shadows, lifted film blacks, fine grain, gentle halation on the blue. The slogan is the only legible text anywhere in the frame: no route number, no plates, no signage. Thanks.
